basis.note: Units follow the six units of BlueDot Impact's Biosecurity course (outline read Nov 2026); laboratory biosafety follows the WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual's risk-based structure and the treaty items follow the BWC's articles. No curriculum standard for biosecurity exists; the objectives are a house list.

big_ideas.title: Defence in depth
big_ideas.text: Prevent, detect, withstand and combat are layers; each fails sometimes, and risk falls by stacking layers whose failures are not correlated.

big_ideas.title: Epidemics are exponential, so time is the currency
big_ideas.text: Doubling times turn days of delay into multiples of cases; every layer is judged by how much time it buys.

big_ideas.title: Norms, rules and safeguards shape what capability becomes
big_ideas.text: Treaties, export controls, screening, oversight and model safeguards narrow who can misuse biology without closing the science.

practices.title: Compute
practices.text: Carry an epidemic, testing, ventilation or countermeasure calculation to a number.

practices.title: Explain
practices.text: Name the institution, rule or mechanism behind a measure.

practices.title: Judge
practices.text: Choose the right measure, layer or response for a scenario, and say what it buys.

los.do: Relate the reproduction number, growth rate, generation interval and doubling time.
ek: T_d = ln 2 / r; with a fixed generation interval T_g, R = e^{rT_g}.

los.do: Compute the herd-immunity threshold from R₀, and R₀ from it.
ek: Threshold = 1 − 1/R₀.

los.do: Distinguish case and infection fatality ratios and correct for under-ascertainment.
ek: CFR = deaths/confirmed cases; IFR = deaths/infections; infections ≈ cases ÷ ascertainment.

los.do: Place landmark events in the history of pandemics and biological weapons.
ek: 1918 influenza; smallpox eradication certified 1980; BWC 1972; Sverdlovsk 1979; the 2001 anthrax letters.

los.do: Distinguish natural, accidental and deliberate biological risks and say what makes a risk catastrophic.
ek: Spillover, lab accident, misuse; transmissibility, severity and our ability to respond set the scale.

los.do: Name the links in the chain of infection and the stages of natural history, and say which measure breaks which link.
ek: Reservoir, portal of exit, transmission, portal of entry, susceptible host; incubation, latent and infectious periods.

los.do: Read an epidemic curve: point source, continuous or propagated, and the likely exposure time.
ek: Point source: one peak about one incubation period wide; exposure ≈ peak − median incubation.

los.do: Compute attack rates and secondary attack rates.
ek: Attack rate = cases ÷ population at risk; secondary attack rate counts contacts of primary cases only.

los.do: Distinguish incidence from prevalence and relate them through duration.
ek: Prevalence ≈ incidence rate × mean duration (steady state).

los.do: Compute a risk ratio or an odds ratio from a 2 × 2 table and say which design gives which.
ek: Cohort: RR = (a/(a+b))/(c/(c+d)); case-control: OR = ad/bc.

los.do: Compute attributable risk and the population attributable fraction.
ek: AR% among exposed = (RR − 1)/RR; PAF = p(RR − 1)/(1 + p(RR − 1)).

los.do: Order the steps of an outbreak investigation and apply case definitions.
ek: Prepare, confirm the outbreak, verify the diagnosis, define and find cases, describe by time, place and person, hypothesise, test, control, communicate.

los.do: Evaluate a surveillance system by sensitivity, predictive value and timeliness.
ek: Sensitivity = cases detected ÷ true cases; PVP = true cases ÷ cases reported.

los.do: Compute the final size of an epidemic and the effective reproduction number as susceptibles fall.
ek: Final size z solves z = 1 − e^{−R₀z}; R_eff = R₀ × susceptible fraction.

los.do: Explain superspreading with the dispersion parameter and compute the chance a case transmits to no one.
ek: Negative binomial offspring: P(0) = (1 + R/k)^{−k}; small k means most cases infect no one and a few infect many.

los.do: State what the BWC prohibits, how it is implemented and reviewed, and what it lacks.
ek: Article I: never develop, produce, stockpile or acquire; no verification regime; confidence-building measures; a small Implementation Support Unit.

los.do: Match export controls and other regimes (Australia Group, UNSCR 1540) to what they do.
ek: Australia Group harmonises national export lists; UNSCR 1540 obliges states to keep WMD from non-state actors.

los.do: Explain DNA synthesis screening: what is screened and why both sequence and customer matter.
ek: Screen orders against sequences of concern and verify customers; benchtop synthesisers move the checkpoint.

los.do: Recognise dual-use research of concern and the oversight and publication choices around it.
ek: Research reasonably expected to give knowledge or products that could be misapplied; review before funding and before publishing.

los.do: Describe layered AI model safeguards and compute the residual risk through independent layers.
ek: Refusal training, input/output classifiers, evaluations, access controls; residual = product of each layer's miss rate.

los.do: Use the WHO risk-based approach: inherent versus residual risk, core requirements, heightened control and maximum containment.
ek: Risk assessment decides the controls; core requirements apply everywhere.

los.do: Choose primary containment (biosafety cabinet class) and compute filter penetration.
ek: Class I protects worker and environment, II also the sample, III is gas-tight; HEPA ≥ 99.97% at the most penetrating size.

los.do: Compute decontamination by log reduction and D-values.
ek: N = N₀·10^{−t/D}; a 6-log kill takes six D-values.

los.do: Place a national capacity in its JEE technical area and pillar.
ek: Prevent P1–P8, Detect D1–D3, Respond R1–R5, plus points of entry, chemical and radiation events.

los.do: Match surveillance systems to what they see and name the IHR's notification duties.
ek: Syndromic, wastewater, metagenomic, clinical; IHR (2005) PHEIC and, since 2025, the pandemic emergency.

los.do: Compute how detection delay translates into cases.
ek: Cases at time t = initial × 2^{t/T_d}.

los.do: Compute the sequencing depth needed to see a target at a given relative abundance.
ek: Expected target reads = total reads × relative abundance.

los.do: Compute the probability that sequencing sees at least one target read.
ek: Reads are Poisson: P(≥ 1) = 1 − e^{−λ}; 95% needs λ ≈ 3.

los.do: Compute predictive values of a test from sensitivity, specificity and prevalence.
ek: PPV falls as prevalence falls; a second independent positive raises it.

los.do: Estimate airborne infection risk with the Wells–Riley model and combine air-cleaning rates.
ek: P = 1 − exp(−Iqpt/Q); equivalent air changes add.

los.do: Explain far-UVC, filtration and ventilation and compute clearance times.
ek: 222 nm barely penetrates the skin's dead layer; 99% removal takes ln 100 / ACH hours.

los.do: Check a room against an equivalent clean airflow per person target.
ek: Total clean air = outdoor air + filtered recirculation × efficiency + air cleaners; ECA per person = total ÷ occupants.

los.do: Compare respirator classes by filtration and assigned protection factor, and compute the effect of masking on R.
ek: N95 filters ≥ 95%; APF 10 half-mask, 50 full-face, 25 loose PAPR; R_eff = R(1 − ce).

los.do: Compute the effect of testing, isolation and contact tracing on R, and match measures to transmission routes.
ek: Removing a fraction f of onward transmission multiplies R by 1 − f.

los.do: Describe rapid countermeasure programmes: platforms, the 100 Days Mission, financing and trials.
ek: CEPI's goal: vaccines within 100 days of a threat; platform technologies; advance commitments.

los.do: Compute the vaccination coverage needed for herd protection given vaccine efficacy.
ek: V_c = (1 − 1/R₀)/E; above 100% means vaccination alone cannot stop spread.

los.do: Compute vaccine efficacy from trial attack rates.
ek: VE = 1 − AR_vaccinated / AR_unvaccinated.

los.do: Compute the number needed to vaccinate and the expected cases averted.
ek: NNV = 1/(AR_unvaccinated × VE).

los.do: Name the global health governance instruments and who decides what.
ek: IHR (2005) and its 2024 amendments; the WHO Pandemic Agreement (2025); the Director-General declares a PHEIC on Emergency Committee advice.

los.do: Compute manufacturing and delivery rates needed to cover a population in time.
ek: Doses per day = population × doses per person ÷ days.

topics.title: Working responsibly and choosing a focus

los.do: Apply information-hazard norms in discussion and writing.
ek: Don't brainstorm new ways to cause harm; discuss defences, not attack details; ask before sharing.

los.do: Map an intervention to its layer and compute the combined protection of independent layers.
ek: P(all layers fail) = product of each layer's failure probability.
